Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Aether Energy Corp Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the question-and-answer session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if you would like to ask a question. To withdraw your question, please press star then two. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Jordan Lee, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Aether Energy Corp's results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on today's call are Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Alex Rivera, Chief Financial Officer; Liam Chen, Chief Development Officer; and Sofia Ramirez, Chief Sustainability Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Jordan, and good morning, everyone. Aether Energy Corp had a strong Q3, reflecting our commitment to innovation and sustainability in the renewable energy sector. We continue to see increasing demand for our clean energy solutions and are well-positioned to capitalize on the growing market opportunities.

Let me kick things off with our overall performance highlights and key achievements for the quarter. I'm thrilled to report that Q3 marked another record-breaking period for Aether Energy Corp, underscoring our leadership in the renewable energy and clean tech space. We delivered revenue of $478 million, up 38% year-over-year and 12% quarter-over-quarter, surpassing our guidance midpoint by 8%. This was driven by a potent mix of strong project executions, favorable module pricing dynamics, and accelerating demand under the U.S. Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) tax credits.

Adjusted EBITDA came in at $142 million, representing a robust 30% margin – our highest Q3 ever – expanding 520 basis points YoY on the back of scale efficiencies and supply chain optimizations. Net income attributable to shareholders was $89 million, or $0.62 per diluted share, beating consensus estimates by $0.07. Free cash flow generation was stellar at $110 million, up 45% YoY, bolstering our balance sheet with $1.2 billion in cash and equivalents and a net debt to EBITDA ratio of just 1.2x.

Operationally, we achieved several milestones that solidify our position as a top-tier integrated player. Our project backlog now stands at a record $6.8 billion, with 85% contracted through 2027, providing exceptional multi-year visibility. We commissioned 1.8 GW of new capacity across solar PV, wind, and hybrid storage projects – that's equivalent to powering over 1.2 million U.S. homes annually. Notably, our VerdantFlow 2.0 bifacial TOPCon modules, with a record 23.1% efficiency certified by NREL, underpinned 60% of these deployments, achieving a levelized cost of energy (LCOE) as low as $22/MWh in sunny U.S. Southwest markets – competitive with, and in some cases below, new-build gas peakers.

On the technical initiatives front, we're pushing the envelope in next-gen clean tech. Our R&D team at the Aether Innovation Campus in Silicon Valley advanced our perovskite-silicon tandem cell prototype to a lab efficiency of 31.2%, on track for commercial pilots in H1 2025. This positions us ahead of peers like Oxford PV and Swift Solar in the race to sub-$0.20/W module costs. In energy storage, we integrated 4.2 GWh of our proprietary AetherStore LFP systems – leveraging CATL-sourced cells with our in-house AI-optimized battery management software (BMS) – into hybrid projects, achieving 95% round-trip efficiency and enabling 4-hour dispatchable power. This is critical as ERCOT and CAISO grids grapple with duck curve challenges.

We're also making strides in green hydrogen, with our first 50 MW electrolyzer project in Texas reaching mechanical completion. Powered by our renewables and using ITM Power's PEM tech, it's contracted to produce H2 at $1.80/kg, benefiting from the full 45V Hydrogen PTC stack – a game-changer as demand surges from industrial off-takers like Air Products.

Regionally, performance was balanced and diversified. In North America, which accounted for 72% of revenue, we capitalized on IRA tailwinds: our 3.5 GW utility-scale pipeline secured $1.2 billion in new PPAs, including a landmark 800 MW deal with Southern California Edison for storage-enhanced solar. Deployment in Texas and Arizona hit 1.2 GW, with interconnection queues advancing 20% faster than industry averages thanks to our FERC-compliant modeling.

Europe contributed 18% of revenue, up 55% YoY, fueled by the EU Green Deal and REPowerEU targets. We flipped 450 MW in Spain and Italy, leveraging our 100% EU-sourced supply chain to qualify for full local content bonuses under the Net-Zero Industry Act. Our Polish wind farm, using Vestas V236-15.0 MW turbines, achieved COD ahead of schedule, capturing high merit-order pricing amid the continent's energy crisis.

In Asia-Pacific and emerging markets (10% of revenue), we expanded via our JV with Adani Green in India, commissioning 300 MW of fixed-tilt solar with 82% capacity factor in Rajasthan – resilient to monsoons via our agrivoltaic designs. In Australia, our 200 MW BESS project in New South Wales supports AEMO's frequency control ancillary services (FCAS), generating $45 million in annual revenues at 150% IRR.

Key achievements beyond the numbers include strategic wins that de-risk our growth trajectory: Closed the $450 million acquisition of BayWa r.e.'s U.S. solar EPC arm, adding 1.2 GW to our development pipeline and vertical integration synergies worth $30 million annually. Renewed our 10 GW module offtake with LONGi Green Energy at locked-in ASPs 15% below spot.

Sustainability leadership: Achieved SBTi-validated net-zero by 2040 targets, with Scope 1&2 emissions down 42% YoY. Our projects avoided 2.1 million metric tons of CO2e, equivalent to removing 450,000 cars from roads.

Policy and market tailwinds: Benefited from $250 million in IRA ITC/PTC transfers, with 90% utilization on domestic content (now at 65% via our Ohio gigafactory ramp). Globally, module prices fell 25% QoQ to $0.18/W, per IRENA data, while lithium carbonate costs dropped 30%, enabling BESS bids at $120/kWh.

Strategically, these results affirm our "Scale, Innovate, Diversify" playbook. We're accelerating capex to $1.5 billion for FY24, targeting 5 GW annual deployments by 2026. Risks like supply chain tariffs and interest rates are mitigated by our hedged 70% of debt at SOFR+150bps and diversified offtake (utilities 60%, corporates 30%, including Google and Amazon RPAs). Looking ahead, Q4 guidance is $510-540 million revenue, $155 million EBITDA, with FY24 consensus affirmed.

We're not just riding the clean energy wave – we're shaping it. Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera to provide a detailed overview of our financial performance.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Elena. We are pleased with our financial results for the Q3. Revenue reached $478 million, representing a 38% increase compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by the successful commissioning of several new projects and higher energy production. Our gross margin improved to 30%, reflecting our efforts to optimize operational efficiency and manage costs effectively. Operating expenses totaled $150 million, primarily due to investments in R&D and expansion into new markets. Net income was $89 million, or $0.62 per share. We maintained a strong balance sheet with $1.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Our financial outlook for the remainder of the year remains positive.

Thank you, Elena, and good morning, everyone. Today, I'd like to dive deeper into one of our core value creation levers: capital recycling through strategic asset sales. As many of you know, in the renewable energy sector, this isn't just about monetizing assets—it's a disciplined playbook for compounding returns. We develop, build, and stabilize high-quality clean energy projects, then recycle proceeds from mature, cash-generative assets into our robust greenfield pipeline. This merchant-plus-PPA model—blending exposure to power price upside with contracted revenues—delivers superior risk-adjusted returns, typically targeting 10-15% unlevered IRRs on the development side, while stabilized assets trade at attractive 7-9x EBITDA multiples in today's market.

Let me start with our Q3 results, which exemplify this strategy in action. I'm pleased to report we closed two marquee transactions totaling $1.75 billion in gross proceeds. First, the divestiture of our 650 MW Southwest U.S. solar portfolio—comprising utility-scale projects like the 300 MW Desert Bloom facility in Arizona and the 200 MW Sagebrush array in Nevada. These assets, built out between 2020 and 2022 with high-efficiency bifacial PERC modules and single-axis trackers, have been operating at fleet-wide capacity factors exceeding 28%, bolstered by our hybrid battery storage integrations totaling 250 MWh. We sold a 100% stake to a leading infrastructure fund consortium, including affiliates of Brookfield Renewable and BlackRock's climate infrastructure platform, at a 1.9x multiple on invested capital and an implied 8.2x forward EBITDA. This generated a $450 million pre-tax gain, with realized IRRs north of 14%—well above our hurdle rates.

Our second transaction was the sale of a 40% minority stake in our 450 MW onshore wind portfolio across the U.K. and Germany. Projects like the 250 MW North Sea Breeze wind farm, featuring Vestas V150-4.2 MW turbines with 15% repowering uplift from our digital wake steering tech, have locked in 12-year CfDs under the U.K.'s AR5 auction regime and Germany's EEG 2023 framework. Proceeds here came in at $850 million, valuing the portfolio at a 9.5x multiple, reflecting strong yieldco appetite amid compressed cap rates of 5.5-6.5% in Europe. Post-sale, we retain majority control and full development economics on adjacent expansions.

Year-to-date, these deals bring our 2024 recycling total to $2.8 billion, up 35% from last year, representing about 25% of our $11 billion development CapEx budget. This disciplined approach has recycled over $12 billion since 2020, funding a pipeline that now stands at 15 GW across solar PV, onshore/offshore wind, and firming storage—positioned for FID in the next 24 months.

Financially, the impact is transformative. These transactions boosted our liquidity to $4.2 billion, including $1.1 billion in undrawn revolvers, giving us ample dry powder for high-conviction bids in upcoming auctions like the U.S. DOE's $7 billion Loan Programs Office tranche or Australia's Capacity Investment Scheme. We recognized $720 million in gains this year, lifting adjusted EBITDA guidance by 12% to $3.6-$3.8 billion. Critically, by selling stabilized assets yielding 8-10% cash-on-cash, we're redeploying at 12-15% IRRs into next-gen opportunities—think 1 GW of tandem perovskite-silicon solar in the U.S. Sun Belt, 500 MW of floating offshore wind off California leveraging our BOEM-approved Crown Estate model, and 800 MWh of long-duration iron-air batteries via our Form Energy JV.

Regionally, the U.S. remains our recycling powerhouse, with IRA-driven PTC/ITC adders pushing solar/wind multiples to 1.8-2.2x amid $270 billion in private capital inflows. Europe, post-REPowerEU, saw 20% YoY multiple expansion for onshore assets, though offshore faces headwinds from supply chain snarls—our selective approach here yielded 15% premium pricing. In APAC, we're piloting sales into Japan's GX funds, where our 200 MW rooftop solar portfolio in Hokkaido fetched a 10x multiple despite yen volatility.

Strategically, this isn't opportunistic—it's baked into our DNA. Unlike pure-play developers chasing volume, our hybrid model mirrors NextEra's playbook but with a cleantech edge: proprietary O&M tech stacks reducing LCOE by 8-10% via AI-driven curtailment optimization, and a focus on hybrid assets capturing the storage megatrend. Market tailwinds are robust—global infrastructure funds have $500 billion in dry powder chasing 6-8% yields, per Preqin data—yet we're selective, targeting only top-quartile assets post-3 years of operations. Going forward, expect 20-25% of annual CapEx funded via recycling, supporting 20%+ EPS CAGR through 2027.

Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining our Q3 earnings call for Aether Energy Corp, where we're reporting another quarter of robust growth in our clean energy portfolio. Today, I'd like to dive deeply into a critical driver of our performance: the impact of government incentives and subsidies. These mechanisms continue to be the bedrock of the renewable energy industry's scalability, accounting for approximately 28% of our adjusted EBITDA this quarter—up from 22% in Q3 2023—while enabling us to accelerate our project pipeline amid falling module prices and improving LCOE profiles.

Let me break this down by key levers, regions, and strategic implications, with specific figures from our books.

United States: IRA Turbocharging Deployment

In the US, the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) of 2022 remains our North Star, with its uncapped Investment Tax Credit (ITC) and Production Tax Credit (PTC)—both extended through 2032 and now featuring 10% domestic content adders and 10% energy community bonuses—directly fueling 65% of our 2.4 GW US backlog. For context, in Q3, we monetized $420 million in transferable ITCs from our 450 MW Desert Sun hybrid solar-plus-storage project in Arizona's Southwest Power Pool (SPP). This included a 50% base ITC bumped to 70% via adders, yielding an effective after-tax yield of 12.8% on invested capital—well above our 9% hurdle rate.

The IRA's clean hydrogen PTC under Section 45V has also unlocked early wins: our 50 MW electrolyzer pilot in Texas, integrated with our wind assets, qualified for up to $3 per kg of H2 produced, adding $15 million to our forward guidance. Without these incentives, the project's LCOE would exceed $40/MWh; with them, it's sub-$25/MWh, competitive with grey hydrogen. We've seen a 35% YoY increase in US EPC bookings, driven by state-level Renewable Portfolio Standards (RPS) in California (60% by 2030) and New York (70% by 2030), where our Clipper Creek offshore wind leasehold positions us for future Orsted-like partnerships.

Europe: Navigating FiTs and REPowerEU Volatility

Across the pond, EU subsidies under the REPowerEU plan and national schemes contributed 18% to our international revenue, or €220 million in Q3. Germany's EEG surcharge reductions and France's new 40% tender bonus for bifacial PERC modules propelled our 300 MW ground-mount portfolio in the Nordics, where feed-in tariffs (FiTs) averaged €65/MWh—bridging the gap as wholesale prices dipped to €45/MWh amid high hydro output.

A highlight was our 150 MW floating PV array on Lake Constance, qualifying for the EU's Innovation Fund grant of €45 million, which covers 60% of CAPEX for next-gen heterojunction (HJT) panels with 23.5% efficiency. This initiative aligns with the Net-Zero Industry Act's domestic manufacturing push, reducing our reliance on Southeast Asian supply chains. However, policy headwinds like the UK's Contracts for Difference (CfD) strike price cuts to £44/MWh in AR5 tenders pressured margins on our East Anglia wind farms, trimming our UK EBITDA contribution by 8% QoQ. Overall, European subsidies de-risked 42% of our 1.2 GW continental pipeline, but we're monitoring Elections in 2024 for potential FiT rollbacks.

Asia-Pacific and Emerging Markets: China and India's Subsidy Surge

In APAC, China's ultra-competitive solar market—now boasting GW-scale TOPCon module production at $0.22/Wp—relies on central and provincial subsidies like the Golden Sun program, which added RMB 180 million ($25 million) to our JV with LONGi Green Energy for a 500 MW tracker system in Inner Mongolia. These incentives, tied to curtailment mitigation via our AI-optimized single-axis trackers (yielding 25% higher yield than fixed-tilt), offset a 15% drop in local PPA prices.

India's PM Surya Ghar rooftop scheme and 50% domestic content mandates under the PLI 2.0 drove a 50% backlog surge to 800 MW, with $110 million in GST rebates and viability gap funding (VGF) for our 200 MW Bhadla Phase III expansion. This positions us ahead of Adani Green peers, as subsidies lower our effective bifacial module cost to ₹18/W ($0.215/W).

Quantitative Impact and Trends

To quantify: incentives boosted our gross margins by 420 bps YoY to 32.5%, with tax equity flips from ITC monetization generating $750 million in non-dilutive capital YTD—funding 60% of our 2025 CAPEX. Our sensitivity analysis shows a 10% IRA adder reduction would shave 150 bps off FY25 EPS, but diversification mitigates this: US exposure is 55%, Europe 25%, APAC 20%.

Trends-wise, global clean tech subsidies hit $1.3 trillion cumulatively per IRENA 2024 data, with a shift from capex grants to performance-based PTCs, favoring our O&M-heavy model. LCOE for utility-scale solar fell 12% to $28/MWh globally, per Lazard's 2024 report, but subsidies remain essential for storage (ITC at 30-50%) and green H2, where unsubsidized costs exceed $5/kg.

Strategic Insights and Forward Outlook

Strategically, we're de-risking subsidy dependency through a three-pillar approach: (1) Geographic diversification—targeting IRA-safe havens like PJM and ERCOT while expanding into Australia's Capacity Investment Scheme; (2) Tech innovation—investing $200 million in perovskite-silicon tandem cells (26.5% lab efficiency) to max domestic content adders; (3) Financial engineering—securitizing tax credits via partnerships with JPMorgan and hedging policy risk with 24-month forward swaps on EU carbon allowances (now at €85/tCO2).

Looking ahead, we expect subsidies to drive 25-30% backlog growth into 2025, with Q4 guidance incorporating $300 million in new IRA/PTC bookings. We're well-positioned as peers like NextEra and Ørsted navigate similar dynamics, but our 15% domestic content ramp (vs. industry 8%) gives us an edge.

Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining Aether Energy Corp's third quarter earnings call. As we dive into our financial results, I'd like to spend some time on a critical pillar of our growth strategy: our approach to tax equity financing and project-level financing. These mechanisms have been instrumental in funding our 2.5 GW development pipeline, enabling us to commission 850 MW of utility-scale solar and storage projects YTD, while maintaining a robust balance sheet with net debt to EBITDA of just 2.8x.

Let me start with tax equity financing, which remains the lifeblood of renewable project economics in the U.S., especially post-Inflation Reduction Act (IRA). For those less familiar, tax equity involves partnering with institutional investors—think large banks like JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, or U.S. Bancorp, alongside yield-hungry insurance giants such as MetLife and Prudential—who have substantial taxable income to shelter. In exchange for injecting capital into our special purpose vehicles (SPVs), they claim the lion's share of federal Investment Tax Credits (ITCs) at 30% base plus up to 10% adders for domestic content and energy communities, or Production Tax Credits (PTCs) at $27/MWh indexed for inflation.

In Q3 alone, we closed $1.4 billion in tax equity commitments across four projects: our 300 MW Gemini Solar + Storage hybrid in Nevada, which flipped at a 7.2% target IRR for investors; the 150 MW Dawn Wind offshore lease off New York, leveraging PTCs under the IRA's transferability provisions; and two battery storage assets totaling 200 MWh in Texas ERCOT, stacking ITCs with the 48C Qualifying Advanced Energy Project Credit. This brings our YTD tax equity raises to $3.2 billion, up 25% year-over-year, outpacing the broader market's 18% growth as reported by the American Clean Power Association (ACP).

Structurally, we employ a standard "flip partnership" model: Tax equity owns 99% of the partnership interests pre-flip, capturing 85-90% of cash flows and all tax benefits until they achieve a 6-8% hurdle IRR—typically 8-10 years post-COD. Post-flip, control reverts to us at a nominal 5% IRR residual, with sponsor distributions kicking in at 12-15% IRR. This has lowered our effective cost of equity to around 4.5% after-tax, versus 9-10% for straight equity. A key trend we're capitalizing on is IRA transferability, which we've used in 30% of deals to cash-sell credits directly, reducing execution risk and attracting non-traditional buyers like Google and Amazon, who've monetized over $5 billion in transferable credits industry-wide this year.

Shifting to project-level financing, this is our non-recourse debt layer, secured solely by project assets, PPAs, and offtake contracts—keeping corporate leverage pristine. We target 55-65% debt leverage at the project level, blending construction loans with tax-exempt bonds and term debt. In Q3, we secured $2.1 billion in project financing at blended all-in costs of LIBOR + 175 bps (now SOFR + 185 bps post-transition), with 15-18 year tenors and 1.4x minimum DSCR covenants.

Break it down by tranche: For construction, we tapped back-leverage facilities from Citi and Goldman Sachs, funding 70% of capex at SOFR + 200 bps during the 18-24 month build phase. Post-COD, we refinance into term B loans from infrastructure funds like Brookfield and AIP, with fixed-rate swaps locking in 4.2-4.5% effective rates amid the Fed's rate cuts. Tax-exempt private activity bonds (PABs) via NY Green Bank and similar state vehicles covered 20% of our Northeast portfolio, yielding sub-3% coupons thanks to volume cap allocations.

Regionally, U.S. Southwest projects like Gemini benefit from CAISO's Resource Adequacy mandates and low-beta PPAs with Southern California Edison at $45/MWh fixed, supporting 60% leverage. In ERCOT, our 100 MW/200 MWh BESS fleet drew ancillary services revenue—$15/kW-year from frequency regulation—boosting cash yields to 14% unlevered IRR, attracting debt from Macquarie. Europe-wise, our 200 MW onshore wind in Ireland secured €300 million in project finance from European Investment Bank (EIB) green loans at Euribor + 125 bps, aligned with REPowerEU's €300 billion mobilization target, though permitting delays pushed two CODs to Q1 '25.

Strategically, the synergy between tax equity and project debt is powering our 5 GW backlog. By layering 40% tax equity, 55% debt, and 5% sponsor equity, we achieve a weighted average cost of capital (WACC) of 4.8%, down 50 bps YoY due to tighter spreads and IRA adders. We're ahead of peers like NextEra—whose tax equity book hit $10B last year—by pioneering hybrid offtake with corporates (e.g., 15-year VPPA with Microsoft at $35/MWh hedged) and tech integrations like LONGi's Hi-MO 7 modules for 22.5% module efficiency, slashing LCOE to $25/MWh.

Challenges? Supply chain headwinds persist—polysilicon tariffs up 20%—but our 2.5 GW domestic content pipeline qualifies for full 10% ITC adder. Interest rate volatility clipped Q3 closings by 10%, but with SOFR at 4.3% and swap curves flattening, we see $5-6B in total financings for '25. This positions us to hit 1.2 GW COD next year, driving AFFO growth of 22% to $450 million.

Now, I'll pass the call to Liam Chen to discuss our project development pipeline.

Liam Chen:
Thank you, Alex. Our project development pipeline continues to grow, with 15 GW of projects under development across various renewable energy technologies. We are making significant progress on securing land rights, obtaining permits, and negotiating power purchase agreements. We expect to bring several new projects online in the coming quarters, which will further contribute to our revenue growth and profitability. We are also exploring opportunities to expand our project portfolio through strategic acquisitions and partnerships.

Capacity factor—or CF—remains a core KPI for us at Aether Energy Corp., as it directly ties to our unlevered IRR and drives merchant upside in competitive markets like ERCOT and CAISO. For Q3, our portfolio-wide blended CF came in at 38.2%, up 210 basis points year-over-year and beating our full-year guidance midpoint of 37.5%. This reflects not just favorable weather but execution on our tech roadmap. Let me break it down by technology, with some color on trends, regions, and our strategic levers.

Starting with solar, which makes up 42% of our 12 GW operating fleet. Q3 fleet-average CF was 27.8%, a solid 160 bps improvement YoY from 26.2%. This was paced by our utility-scale fixed-tilt and tracker assets. Single-axis trackers, now on 68% of our new builds like the 450 MW Mojave Sunburst project, delivered 31-33% CF in the Southwest—think Arizona and Nevada hubs—thanks to our DC:AC ratios optimized at 1.35:1 and bifacial modules from LONGi hitting 22.5% efficiencies. In contrast, Northeast sites like our 200 MW Empire State array averaged 22.4% due to lower insolation and winter cloud cover, but we're mitigating with our AI-driven irradiance forecasting from Clir Renewables, which shaved 2% off curtailment.

Key trend here: Panel degradation has stabilized at 0.4% annually across our 5+ year fleet, below the industry 0.5% benchmark from NREL data. Looking ahead, we're deploying heterojunction (HJT) tech in our 1 GW 2025 pipeline, targeting 29-30% CF uplift, especially in hybrid solar+storage co-locs where we capture evening peaks.

Moving to wind, our largest segment at 48% of capacity with 5.8 GW onshore and 1.2 GW offshore. Onshore CF averaged 41.7% in Q3—up 180 bps YoY—led by our Midwest fleet in SPP and MISO territories. Sites like the 300 MW Prairie Winds repower in Oklahoma hit 44.5% with Vestas V150-4.2 MW turbines featuring 155m rotors, benefiting from stronger shear exponents post our SCADA upgrades. Offshore, our East Coast lease areas off Virginia and New York delivered 49.2% CF, on par with Orsted's Hornsea benchmarks, though wake losses capped us at 47% in array-heavy blocks.

Regional nuance: Texas ERCOT wind dipped to 38% amid low-resource summer lulls, but our hybrid pairing with storage—now 25% of wind assets—boosted effective output by arbitraging 4-hour discharges during net peak hours. Initiatives driving this? Our $150M capex in leading-edge blade tech from LM Wind Power and digital twins via WindESCo, which improved AEP by 5% fleet-wide. Degradation is minimal at 1.2% annually, and we're on track for 43% onshore CF guidance in '25 via 800 MW of V236-15 MW installs.

Finally, storage, our fastest-growing at 10% of EBITDA from 2.5 GWh deployed, mostly 4-hour lithium iron phosphate (LFP) packs from CATL and Tesla Megapack clones. Here, we're focusing on utilization factor—energy discharged over nameplate—as a proxy for CF, which hit 68% in Q3, up from 62% YoY. Round-trip efficiency (RTE) held steady at 92.3%, with calendar aging at just 1.8% capacity fade per year, beating our 2.5% warranty targets.

Breakout: Frequency regulation in PJM pushed 85% utilization on our 200 MWh Philly Battery, while ERCOT arbitrage fleets averaged 55% dispatch factor amid heatwaves, capturing $250/MWh spreads. California sites faced 10% curtailment from duck curve dynamics, but our virtual power plant (VPP) software from AutoGrid optimized stacking revenues—35% ancillary, 45% energy arb, 20% capacity. Strategically, we're shifting to 100-hour iron-air flow batteries from Form Energy for our 500 MWh pilots, eyeing 75%+ utilization in winter-peaking regions like the Northeast.

Strategically, these CF gains underscore our "high-CF core" thesis: we're prioritizing Tier 1 wind regimes (>9 m/s capacity factor wind speed) and GHI >2,200 kWh/m² solar sites, with 70% of our 8 GW development pipeline in such zones. Hybrids are key—solar+wind+storage combos lifted blended CF by 400 bps in pilots—and PPAs now include CF floors tied to our O&M SLAs. Marginally, every 100 bps CF uplift adds $15M to annual EBITDA at current power prices.

Forward guidance: Q4 blended CF at 39%, full-year 38.5%. Risks are weather volatility and supply chain for trackers/blades, but hedges and our $2B liquidity position us well.

Next, Sofia Ramirez will provide an update on our sustainability initiatives.

Sofia Ramirez:
Thank you, Liam. Sustainability is at the core of our business, and we are committed to reducing our environmental footprint and contributing to a cleaner, more sustainable future. We have made significant progress in reducing our carbon emissions, improving our energy efficiency, and promoting responsible resource management. We are also actively involved in community engagement and supporting local initiatives that promote sustainability. We believe that our sustainability efforts not only benefit the environment but also create long-term value for our stakeholders.

I'll now turn the call back to Elena for closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Sofia. In conclusion, we are very pleased with our performance this quarter. We are confident that our strategic initiatives and our commitment to innovation and sustainability will drive continued growth and success in the years to come.

Operator, let's proceed with the Q&A session.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Sarah Jenkins with GreenCapital Partners. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter, team. Could you dive deeper into capacity factor performance by technology—solar, wind, and storage? Specifically, how are you tracking against your guidance, any regional variances, and what initiatives are driving improvements?

Liam Chen:
Absolutely, Sarah, great question and timely as we just wrapped our Q3 asset optimization review. [Liam Chen delivers the capacity factor details as above, but since already in prepared remarks, he references: As I mentioned earlier in my remarks, our portfolio-wide blended CF... and recaps key points briefly for emphasis, ensuring full coverage.]

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Torres with Greenstreet Advisors. Please go ahead.

Mike Torres:
What is your strategy for expanding into emerging markets?

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks for the question, Mike. Our expansion into emerging markets is a key growth driver, particularly in APAC where subsidies like China's Golden Sun program and India's PM Surya Ghar scheme have supercharged our backlog. We've seen a 50% surge in India to 800 MW through JVs like with Adani Green, leveraging VGF and domestic content mandates to drop costs. Similarly, in Australia, our BESS projects tap FCAS revenues. We diversify geographically to de-risk, pairing this with tech like AI trackers for higher yields, while hedging currency and policy risks. This supports 25-30% backlog growth into 2025.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Grant with EcoInvest Partners. Please go ahead.

Lisa Grant:
How are you managing the increasing competition in the renewable energy sector?

Elena Vasquez:
Great question, Lisa. Competition is intensifying, but our hybrid model—combining development, recycling, and proprietary tech—sets us apart. We focus on top-quartile assets with high CFs, domestic content for IRA adders, and selective recycling at premium multiples, like our recent 1.9x solar sale. Unlike volume-chasers, we target 12-15% IRRs via O&M optimizations reducing LCOE 8-10%, and hybrids capturing storage trends. With $4.2B liquidity and partnerships like LONGi and Form Energy, we're ahead on next-gen like perovskites and long-duration storage, ensuring margin expansion amid peers' pressures.

Operator:
Thank you. There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Elena Vasquez for any closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you all for your participation in today's call. We appreciate your continued support of Aether Energy Corp. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
